ossec_alerts.broad_spectrum_reason: Unlike CrowdStrike/Defender, this is NOT vendor-native dynamic tagging exceeding a fixed list - it's the opposite. The base/default OSSEC ruleset does not ship with MITRE ATT&CK mapping (confirmed via a 2019 GitHub issue on wazuh-ruleset asking whether OSSEC rules would ever be mapped to ATT&CK IDs, and the existence of separate third-party rulesets built specifically to add that mapping after the fact). A fixed technique list would be inaccurate to assign without adopting one of those supplemental rulesets first - this entry reflects a real capability gap in the base tool, not analytical breadth.

detections.broad_spectrum_reason: Vendor-native per-detection MITRE ATT&CK tagging: CrowdStrike's own certification materials confirm 'Falcon maps detections to this taxonomy' at alert-generation time, and CrowdStrike's MITRE ATT&CK Evaluation results show detection coverage spanning nearly the entire framework. A fixed technique list here would understate real coverage, not describe it accurately - each detection carries its own specific tag dynamically, assigned by the vendor's detection engine, not by this catalog.

device_alerts.broad_spectrum_reason: Same reasoning as CrowdStrike Falcon detections: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint alerts carry vendor-native MITRE ATT&CK tagging assigned per-alert, not a fixed technique set this catalog could enumerate without understating true coverage.
